verdict.root_cause: The failure is in frontend, not cart. A platform-automation loop repeatedly set and reverted frontend's CART_ADDR to the non-default cart:7071 [tr_ed2569452a0f]; the frontend process restarted at 02:20:45 with that override in effect and immediately logged gRPC UNAVAILABLE / connection refused to 172.18.0.24:7071 [tr_aa892a5f8284], and frontend's error ratio steps up at ~02:24 and stays roughly 3.2x baseline through the window [tr_3bcd8e1caa10]. Cart itself is healthy throughout - zero error spans across the whole window and normal ValkeyCartStore request handling at both ends of it [tr_786233993bff][tr_9274dd528586] - and has no change records at all [tr_3209582a64a7]. The 06:07 alert on cart, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator is therefore the caller-side propagation of frontend's wrong cart endpoint value, not a cart fault. The wrong address value is itself the mechanism: requests to that port are refused.
verdict.reasoning: Cart is excluded as origin: flat-zero error ratio with zero variance across 489 incident samples and an identically clean baseline [tr_786233993bff], plus info-only store operations bookending the window [tr_9274dd528586], and no changes on record [tr_3209582a64a7]. That leaves the caller. Frontend is the only service with both a recorded change and a measured error shift: the sole key ever touched is the cart address [tr_ed2569452a0f], the process restarted at 02:20 and refused connection to port 7071 three seconds later [tr_aa892a5f8284], and the single detected change point in the error ratio is ~02:24 - minutes after that restart [tr_3bcd8e1caa10]. The mechanism is a configuration value naming a port nothing is listening on, which is bad_config rather than a dependency being slow or down: cart answers normally for every other caller. Confidence is low because the change log says the override was reverted ~3.6h before onset and the specialist ruled it in effect at onset [tr_ed2569452a0f], and no frontend log or trace covers 06:07 at all [tr_aa892a5f8284][tr_75d59e0690c2] - so the link between the 02:24 shift and the 06:07 alert is inferred, not observed.
open_questions: Was CART_ADDR actually in effect in the running frontend process at 06:07? The change log records a revert at 02:29 but the process started at 02:20 and may hold the boot-time value regardless of later reverts - a direct read of the running environment would settle this.

Why does frontend emit no logs after 05:13:23 and no traces after 05:59:23 [tr_aa892a5f8284][tr_75d59e0690c2]? This could be a crash, a log-pipeline break, or sampler truncation; if frontend actually stopped, process_freeze becomes a live candidate.
What happened at 06:07 specifically? Every frontend signal predates it; the alert time is unexplained by any measured onset.
The NOT_FOUND cluster against product-catalog at 05:13 [tr_aa892a5f8284] is unexplained and may be a second, independent fault.
checkout alerted a minute later and was never dispatched on.

alternatives.root_cause: The frontend process stopped serving around 06:00-06:07 while its socket still accepted, so callers hung and alerted while frontend wrote nothing.
alternatives.why_not: Fits the simultaneous silence in logs after 05:13 and traces after 05:59, but neither gap is confirmed to be the service rather than the telemetry pipeline, and frontend's error ratio kept producing samples through the window [tr_3bcd8e1caa10], which a frozen process would not.

alternatives.root_cause: A downstream dependency of frontend (product-catalog most plausibly) degraded and frontend surfaced the failures as errors to its callers.
alternatives.why_not: Sampled traces show every downstream, including the product-catalog SQL child, returning in single-digit milliseconds right up to 05:59 [tr_75d59e0690c2], and the 05:13 errors are application-level NOT_FOUND from a reachable service [tr_aa892a5f8284] - no waiting is in evidence. No dispatch covered product-catalog directly, so this is not eliminated.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric is expected. The current state should persist: frontend error ratio remaining near the ~0.035 incident-window mean and cart error ratio remaining at zero, pending a direct read of frontend's running environment (docker inspect / env dump) and a check of whether frontend is still exporting logs and traces after 05:13/05:59.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if a direct read of the running frontend process shows CART_ADDR=cart:7071 still in effect AND frontend logs show recurring connection-refused to port 7071 after the 02:20 boot line. Neither is in evidence: the single refused connection to 172.18.0.24:7071 is a one-off three seconds after process start [tr_aa892a5f8284], and the change log records the override reverted to unset at 02:29, 3.6h before onset, with no re-application [tr_ed2569452a0f]. It would also be wrong if frontend has in fact stopped serving entirely — but the error-ratio series carries 969 non-null samples through the window [tr_3bcd8e1caa10], which means spans were still being produced, so a dead-process story is not supported and restart_service's precondition (evidence pointing at process state) is not met.
proposal.risk: The named fix class, revert_config on frontend, is actively dangerous here. frontend's recorded prior configuration IS the override CART_ADDR=cart:7071; the current state is already the reverted/unset one [tr_ed2569452a0f]. Executing revert_config would therefore re-apply the bad cart address and recreate the container — manufacturing the exact failure the verdict describes, on a service that is currently carrying traffic. Proposing it on low confidence would convert a partly-understood 3.2x error elevation into a certain cart-path outage.
proposal.blast_radius: Had an action been taken on frontend, the recreate would reset connections for frontend-proxy and load-generator (its inbound callers in this incident) and move or break traffic to cart, product-catalog, product-reviews, recommendation, ad and, via checkout, currency, payment, shipping and email. Cart is demonstrably healthy — zero error spans across 489 samples and normal ValkeyCartStore handling through 06:09:16 [tr_786233993bff][tr_9274dd528586] — so any disruption there would be self-inflicted. Abstaining leaves all of these untouched.
proposal.notes_for_reader: Three unresolved items block any proposal: (1) the measured error onset is ~02:24, nearly four hours before the 06:07 alert [tr_3bcd8e1caa10], so no permitted action is aimed at the thing that fired the alert; (2) the NOT_FOUND cluster against product-catalog at 05:13 [tr_aa892a5f8284] is a plausible second, independent fault that no proposed action addresses; (3) the frontend log gap after 05:13 and trace gap after 05:59 [tr_aa892a5f8284][tr_75d59e0690c2] are unexplained and may be observability-pipeline rather than service failures. The cheapest next step is diagnostic, not remedial: read the running frontend environment directly and confirm whether its log/trace export is alive.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Five services alerted near-simultaneously across cart, frontend, proxy and checkout, which is a multi-service user-path failure rather than a single quiet latency warning. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alerts give no clear signature of a specific fault class.
